evals.expected_output: For a small, non-separable feature (everything funnels through one shared module), the skill emits a single plan covering the whole canvas instead of forcing a split.
evals.setup: Generate a canvas with /spdd-canvas for a small feature where all Operations touch the same file/module.
assertions: Exactly one file is created under plans/
The plan's Operations cover the full canvas, not a subset
The plan's 'Depends on:' field is 'none'
The plan file's header links back to ../canvas.md
The report explains why the work was kept as a single plan

evals.expected_output: For a feature whose Operations clearly belong to two independent modules with no file overlap, the skill produces two plans with 'Depends on: none' on both.
evals.setup: Generate a canvas for a feature with two clearly separable concerns (e.g. a new entity plus an unrelated notification integration).
assertions: Two files are created under plans/
Each plan lists a disjoint subset of Structure paths
Both plans declare 'Depends on: none'
The report shows the dependency graph with no edges between the two plans

evals.expected_output: For a feature where part B genuinely needs a field or entity introduced by part A, the skill produces plans where plan B declares 'Depends on: plan-01' (or the correct id).
evals.setup: Generate a canvas for a feature where one Operation set depends on an Entity/field only introduced by another Operation set.
assertions: At least one plan has a non-'none' 'Depends on:' field
The dependency referenced actually exists as another plan id
The report's dependency graph reflects this edge

evals.expected_output: When two otherwise-independent plans both need to edit the same shared file (e.g. a central router or providers registry), both plans list it under 'Shared touchpoints:'.
evals.setup: Generate a canvas for a feature where two separable parts both need to register something in the same central file.
assertions: The shared file appears under 'Shared touchpoints:' in both plans that touch it
The plans are still otherwise treated as independent (no forced 'Depends on' just because of the shared touchpoint)

evals.expected_output: A plans/ folder already exists with a plan whose Status is Implemented. Running spdd-design again does not silently overwrite it — the skill warns explicitly and requires confirmation before touching anything.
evals.setup: Run spdd-design once to produce plan-01, mark plan-01 'Status: Implemented', then run spdd-design again on the same change without confirming anything.
assertions: The skill does not overwrite plan-01.md before the user responds
The response explicitly warns that plan-01 has progress (Implemented) that would be discarded
plan-01.md's content and Status are unchanged unless the user explicitly confirmed an overwrite

evals.prompt: /spdd-design (canvas already in English; the user gives spdd-design additional instructions in Spanish while it runs, e.g. 'agrupa todo en un solo plan')
evals.expected_output: The generated plan-*.md stays entirely in English — plan name, section headings, and all newly authored prose in Operations/Entities/Structure — even though the user's mid-run instructions were in Spanish. No mixing of Spanish and English within the document.
evals.setup: Generate a canvas with /spdd-canvas (already in English per this version). Run /spdd-design on it, but phrase any follow-up instruction to the agent in Spanish.
assertions: plan-*.md's plan name, headings, and body content are entirely in English
No Spanish words appear in newly authored prose (Operations/Entities/Structure descriptions, Depends on/Shared touchpoints notes)
Content copied verbatim from the canvas's Operations table remains unchanged and consistent in English
The Step 7 language note in spdd-design/SKILL.md is followed regardless of the conversation language used to invoke the skill
